pr.title: Add and remove a loop's pull requests through the CLI
pr.head: 4f6f9f52346c4c65ae726333c7b17d7cca4e9e6b

summary: A watch loop or a review loop keeps the pull requests it works on in a tracked file: a plain text file the loop's watcher script re-reads every cycle, with one owner/repo#number per line. A line that starts with !, such as !acme/app#12, is an exclusion: it keeps that pull request out of the loop wherever it sits in the file. Two CLI commands already changed the file: project loop drop appends an exclusion, and project loop restore deletes one.

Every other write was done by hand. The loop skills told the agent running the loop to write the tracked set at the start, to append each pull request it created, adopted, or was assigned, and to delete a line when its pull request merged or closed. This change adds project loop add and project loop remove for those writes, and points every skill instruction, watcher message, and document at them.

CommandLines it changesWhen a loop runs it
add (new)Appends owner/repo#number, creating the fileTo bring a pull request into the loop
remove (new)Deletes the plain lines, keeps the ! linesWhen a pull request merges or closes
dropAppends !owner/repo#numberTo keep an open pull request out
restoreDeletes the ! linesTo let a dropped pull request back in

The two new commands respect exclusions on purpose. remove leaves a ! line in place, and add refuses a pull request that has one, so only restore undoes a drop. The review loop's watcher adopts the operator's open pull requests by appending any the file does not name, and it treats an exclusion as naming one, so a dropped pull request is never adopted again if it reopens.

cards.title: What the change leaves alone
cards.html:
• The review watcher's adoption still appends lines itself. That write belongs to the watcher, not to an agent.
  • Exclusions for closed pull requests stay in the file. Only restore deletes them.

groups.title: The add and remove commands
groups.kicker: Two project loop commands that list a pull request and forget a finished one
intro: src/projector/loop.py holds the tracked-file commands. They write the file in two ways. An append adds a line at the end without rewriting the file, because the review watcher may be appending an adopted pull request at the same moment. A rewrite goes through write_through, the repository's atomic write that swaps in a temporary file and keeps the original's mode and any symlink.

• add appends through append, a helper it now shares with drop. It creates the file and its directory when they are missing, changes nothing when the file already lists the pull request, and refuses with exit 65 a pull request the file drops, naming project loop restore in its message.
  • remove rewrites through rewrite_without, the former body of restore, which now takes the line test as an argument. restore passes is_exclusion for ! lines, and remove passes the new is_entry for plain lines. When nothing matches, the file is not rewritten.

Both match the reference without regard to case, and check it with the same pattern the watchers use for an entry, so neither writes a line a watcher reports as malformed. In src/projector/cli.py, run_loop replaces its drop-or-restore branches with one table keyed by the subcommand, giving each command its function, its --json action, and its two messages.

checks.text: The new AddTests and RemoveTests and the existing drop and restore tests all pass on this head. Manual runs through a symlink rewrote or created the link's target and kept the link.

files.note: Adds append, add, is_entry, rewrite_without, and remove; drop and restore now call the shared helpers.

checks.text: The exclusion check runs before the entry check, so a file holding both acme/app#2 and !acme/app#2 refuses too, and the file is left as it was.

A watcher may append a line it adopted while this rewrite runs, and the rename would then lose that line. restore had the same window at the base, and the hand edit this replaces had it too. The review watcher re-adopts a lost line on its next cycle, because it appends every open pull request the file does not name.
The docstring states why exclusions survive: a review loop would otherwise adopt a dropped pull request again if it reopened.

groups.title: Loop skills and watchers
groups.kicker: Every place that told a loop to write a tracked line by hand now runs a command
intro: Two skills run loops over a tracked file: start-watch-loop, which fixes review findings on pull requests, and start-review-loop, which reviews each new head. A third, implement, hands a new pull request to a running watch loop. All three now build and grow the set with project loop add and drop finished pull requests with project loop remove, and both loop skills name the four commands and say how they differ.

Two behaviors follow from the commands. The watch watcher refuses a tracked file it cannot read, so the watch loop now starts its watcher only once add has created the file. And a TRACKED event, which the watchers print once for a line they cannot use, now gets a specific answer: remove a line that names no pull request with project loop remove, and tell the user about a malformed line, which no project loop command writes.

The watcher scripts change only in comments and messages. Both say "remove it from the tracked file" in their not-found TRACKED event, and the review watcher says it in its CLOSED event instead of "drop it", because drop is the command that keeps an open pull request out.

checks.text: A search of the head finds no remaining instruction to write, append, or delete a tracked line by hand.

files.note: Step 4 builds the set with add and starts the watcher once the file exists; closing, idle, and DONE handling run remove.
